articles.title: Deadly high-speed train collision in Spain
articles.description: At least 39 people have been killed after two high-speed trains collided near Urda, Spain.

articles.headline: Finland and Norway leaders discuss Ukraine peace efforts in rare call with Putin
articles.title: Norway and Finland leaders hold rare call with Putin
articles.summary: The leaders of Finland and Norway held a ninety-minute call with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss diplomatic efforts regarding the war in Ukraine. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stre stated the initiative aimed to convey direct messages on future peace negotiations. The Kremlin reported Putin emphasized that a lasting peace requires considering Russia's interests.
articles.description: An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Finland's President Alexander Stubb said.

articles.headline: Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash
articles.title: Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash
articles.description: People have been killed after a Spanish high-speed train collided with another train south of the capital Madrid, making this the country's worst disaster since 2013.

articles.headline: Ethiopia acquires twelve Russian fighter jets and plans air defense purchase
articles.title: Ethiopia receives 12 Russian Su-35 jets, plans S-400 acquisition
articles.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the delivery of twelve Su-35 fighter jets from Moscow during the Russia-Africa Summit on Wednesday. The aircraft arrived ahead of schedule to help Ethiopian armed forces defend airspace and deter aggression amid ongoing domestic conflicts in Tigray and Amhara regions. The prime minister also stated that the country will purchase four S-400 batteries.
articles.description: PM Abiy Ahmed makes announcement during a Moscow summit as Ethiopia battles armed groups in Tigray and Amhara.

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab kills five people and batters north Andhra Pradesh with heavy rain
articles.title: 5 dead as Cyclone Arnab batters north Andhra with heavy rain
articles.summary: Severe Cyclonic Storm Arnab caused five fatalities and widespread damage across north Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28, 2026, according to official reports. Packing winds up to 150 kmph, the storm uprooted over 1,000 trees and flooded agricultural land across 80,500 hectares. Chief Minister N. Chandravabu Naidu announced relief packages including rice and essential food items for affected families.
articles.description: Extremely heavy rain and winds gusting up to 150 kmph lash coastal districts; over 1,000 trees uprooted, crops across 80,500 hectares affected

articles.headline: India faces structural challenges and middle-income trap amid weak job creation
articles.title: The way out of the dangerous trap
articles.summary: India is drifting toward a middle-income trap characterized by weak job creation, stagnant wages, sluggish private investment, and low productivity, threatening its rise to high-income status. Structural issues stem from institutions shaped by social norms that undervalue vocational education and manual skills. Chief Economic Adviser V Anantha Nageswaran recently urged youth to pursue trades instead of chasing software roles.
articles.description: India risks a middle-income, low-productivity trap as weak job creation, stagnant wages and sluggish investment reinforce one another; escaping it requires better vocational education, wider diffusion of technology and useful knowledge, and greater social value for skilled work

articles.headline: Government notifies personal details required for the 2027 Census population enumeration
articles.title: The concerns over the Census questions
articles.summary: The Central government notified the individual questions for the population enumeration phase of the 2027 Census last month. In a significant departure from previous surveys, respondents must provide parents and spouse details, declared nationality, permanent residential address, COVID-19 vaccination place, bank accounts, mobile numbers, Aadhaar, Voter ID, passport, and driving license availability.
articles.description: The questionnaire for the population enumeration phase of the 2027 Census comprises 40 questions and seek details such as nationality, number of bank accounts and mobile, Aadhaar and voter ID numbers, if available, raising concerns over its potential digression from the purpose of collecting data for policy and planning

articles.headline: Kremlin excludes European countries from upcoming talks with Ukraine and the United States
articles.title: Kremlin says European countries not included in next Ukraine talks
articles.summary: European nations will not participate in the upcoming discussions between Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi, according to Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov. While Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv wants European involvement, differing accounts emerged regarding the trilateral meetings. Meanwhile, the Netherlands and Britain announced substantial new military and financial support packages for Ukraine.
articles.description: The comment comes as UK and Netherlands pledge extra military support for Kyiv.

articles.headline: Jio Platforms debuts strongly on stock exchanges amid broader market decline
articles.title: Jio Platforms debuts at 21% premium as Sensex slides; valuation tops ₹12 lakh crore
articles.summary: Jio Platforms Limited made a strong stock market debut on October 28, 2026, listing at 1,358 rupees for a 21.36 percent premium. Managing Director Akash Ambani noted the IPO was subscribed over 22 times. The market capitalization reached approximately 12.5 lakh crore rupees, making it India's second-most-valued listed company behind parent Reliance Industries.
articles.description: With a market capitalisation of around ₹12.5 lakh crore, JPL overtook Bharti Airtel to become India’s second-most-valued listed company after parent Reliance Industries.

articles.headline: Analysis highlights significant gap in official manufacturing sector GVA estimates
articles.title: The gap in manufacturing sector GVA
articles.summary: The National Statistical Office reported manufacturing gross value added at 38.6 lakh crore rupees for 2023-24 at current prices. An alternative estimate using official Annual Survey of Industries and Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises data sets the figure at 27.4 lakh crore rupees. This leaves an unexplained gap of 24.5 percent even after accounting for residual workers.
articles.description: According to the National Accounts Statistics, the manufacturing sector’s GVA is ₹38.6 lakh crore in 2023-24 at current prices.; however, an ‘Alternative Estimate’ using data from the Annual Survey of Industries and Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises gives a lower figure, prompting a closer look at the official estimate

articles.headline: Health experts criticize excessive cancer drug pricing following revised price lists
articles.title: Sharp cuts in price of cancer drugs expose excessive pricing, say health experts
articles.summary: Medical health activists stated on October 28, 2026, that revised Maximum Retail Price lists for anti-cancer medicines published by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority expose excessive pricing. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority released 543 brand prices effective November 9 following Trade Margin Rationalization. Activists argued that trade margin caps alone are insufficient to ensure affordability.
articles.description: NPPA releases revised MRPs for 543 brands of anti-cancer medicines with the new prices effective from November 9; Jan Swasthya Abhiyan India (JSA India) says controlling trade margins alone is insufficient as life-saving cancer treatment must be affordable based on medical need, not a patient’s ability to pay

articles.headline: Ten people die in collision involving two high-speed trains in Toledo province
articles.title: More than 60 dead after two trains collide in Spain’s Toledo Province
articles.summary: At least ten people died following a collision between two trains in central Spain on October 28, 2026. According to rail operator ADIF, the crash occurred in Toledo province, disrupting services between Madrid, Ciudad Real, and Andalusia. State broadcaster TVE reported that one high-speed train struck the rear of another traveling in the same direction, causing carriages to derail.
articles.description: The accident was between two high-speed trains carrying hundreds of passengers and heading in the same direction from the capital, Madrid, to Seville in southwestern Spain

articles.headline: Train collision in Spain leaves at least 30 people dead
articles.title: What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash
articles.summary: At least 30 people died when two trains collided south of Madrid on Wednesday morning, according to local media citing the regional government. State-owned Renfe and private operator Iryo trains crashed between Mora and Orgaz at around 09:00 local time, carrying over 500 passengers combined. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and the royal family expressed shock while emergency services deployed helicopters and fire crews to the scene.
articles.description: More than 500 passengers were on board the trains when the incident occurred in the province of Toledo, south of Madrid.

articles.headline: Bolsonaro turns up in Florida after vanishing from public view
articles.title: Bolsonaro turns up in Florida after vanishing from public view
articles.description: Flavio Bolsonaro, Brazil’s defeated presidential candidate, landed in Florida after fleeing the country with his family.

articles.headline: Israeli president hopes to avoid new vote after inconclusive election results
articles.title: Israel president urges against new vote despite inconclusive result
articles.summary: President Isaac Herzog expressed hope on October 28, 2026, for avoiding a second election after an inconclusive vote on October 27 left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot short of a majority. Netanyahu's bloc is projected to win 53 seats and Eisenkot's opposition 48 in the 120-seat parliament, with Arab lists projected to reach 19 seats.
articles.description: With more than 85% of ballots counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority in the election

articles.headline: Flavio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami following his presidential election defeat in Brazil
articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after losing Brazil’s presidential election
articles.summary: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami, Florida, on Wednesday morning after he lost the presidential election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Brazil's Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passports to prevent him from fleeing potential embezzlement and money laundering investigations before his senatorial immunity ended in January.
articles.description: Bolsonaro and his family fled to the US amid a Brazilian Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.

articles.headline: Israel faces political deadlock as election results leave both leading blocs without majorities
articles.title: How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
articles.summary: Following Tuesday's election in Israel, neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition nor challenger Gadi Eisenkot's bloc secured a parliamentary majority with 85% of votes counted. Potential resolutions include a national unity government, an opposition coalition reliant on Arab parties, right-wing defections to Netanyahu, or holding new elections, a recurring outcome between 2019 and 2022.
articles.description: With 85% of votes counted, all signs point to an impasse. The most likely outcome may be new elections.

articles.headline: Israel's election result is messy - here's why
articles.title: Israel's election result is messy - here's why
articles.description: Despite having the highest voter turnout in nearly three decades, Israel's elections have had no clear winner. What does this mean for the country, asks the BBC's Yolande Knell.

articles.headline: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi meets Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus
articles.title: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi meets Ahmed al-Sharaa in historic Syria visit
articles.summary: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi traveled to Damascus to meet Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa in the first such visit since Bashar al-Assad fell. According to the Iraqi News Agency, the leaders discussed expanding economic, oil, and agricultural cooperation, including exporting Iraqi oil through the Baniyas line following the outbreak of the United States-led war on Iran.
articles.description: Talks focused on enhancing trade, reviving Baniyas oil pipeline and achieving stability through cooperation.

articles.headline: Israeli election results show no clear winner as Arab minority parties hold potential balance of power
articles.title: Israeli Arab parties hold key as Netanyahu falls short of majority
articles.summary: Results from the October 27, 2026 election showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc leading with 54 seats against opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's 49 seats, both falling short of the 61-seat majority. Arab minority lists projected to win 17 seats could influence government formation, while both leaders signaled potential military actions regarding Iran alongside United States President Donald Trump.
articles.description: With more than three-quarters of the vote counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was slightly ahead but still short of a majority

articles.headline: Tens of thousands flee Ethiopia fighting into neighbouring Kenya
articles.title: Tens of thousands flee Ethiopia fighting into neighbouring Kenya
articles.description: Tens of thousands of people have crossed into Kenya, fleeing fighting between regional forces in Ethiopia’s Moyale town.

articles.headline: Record turnout marks inconclusive Israeli election as parties weigh coalition and Arab alliances
articles.title: Israel’s election: The battle between change and anti-Palestinian sentiment
articles.summary: Voter turnout reached 77.7 percent in Tuesday's election, the highest since 1999, as outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition secured 54 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition won 49 seats. With neither bloc reaching the 61-seat majority, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders to determine who receives the mandate to form a government within 28 days.
articles.description: With both blocs short of a majority, parties face a choice: to break the taboo on Arab allies or return to the polls.

articles.headline: Israeli leaders claim mandates following inconclusive general election
articles.title: Netanyahu and rival each claim mandate after tight Israel election
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition challenger Gadi Eisenkot both vowed to form a government on October 28, 2026, following a general election featuring a turnout of nearly 78 percent. Exit polls showed both major blocs securing approximately 51 seats, falling short of the 61-seat majority required in parliament and raising the possibility of protracted coalition talks.
articles.description: Exit polls showed Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc neck and neck with Mr. Netanyahu’s hard-right camp and both well away from the threshold for a majority in Parliament

articles.headline: Supreme Court directs the Election Commission to simplify Delhi enrolment
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court asks ECI to extend deadlines, simplify enrolment
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India instructed the Election Commission of India on Wednesday to extend deadlines for the special intensive revision of electoral rolls in Delhi and simplify voter enrolment. The bench emphasized that Form 6 remains unchanged and granted two weeks for adjustments, noting there is currently no election taking place in the national capital.
articles.description: While addressing the ECI in the Delhi SIR case, the top court clarified that it did not judicially review the ‘logical discrepancy’ in the Bihar SIR case

articles.headline: Hackers target US Federal Election Commission website ahead of midterms
articles.title: Hackers target US campaign finance system days before midterm elections
articles.summary: Unidentified hackers targeted the United States Federal Election Commission website, forcing a temporary suspension of web-facing services days before the midterm elections. The outage disrupted the filing of critical 24 and 48-hour spending reports that track political financing. Democratic Commissioner Dara Lindenbaum confirmed systems are being restored, while officials emphasized that voter files and registration databases managed by individual states remain completely unaffected.
articles.description: An FEC email said a 'bad actor' tried to breach its systems as the US prepares for its most expensive elections ever.

articles.headline: Benjamin Netanyahu leads in Israel election after partial vote count
articles.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a narrow lead with 55 of 120 parliament seats after fifty percent of votes were counted on October 28, 2026. His rival Gadi Eisenkot secured forty-nine seats, while Arab parties claimed sixteen. Neither bloc reached a majority, prompting expectations of extended coalition negotiations or potential new elections following the general vote.
articles.description: After 51.8% of ballots were counted, Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc was shown to have 55 of the 120 seats in the parliament; partial results suggest that Eisenkot-led Opposition bloc would have enough seats for a majority if there was a coalition agreement with the Arab parties

articles.headline: South Korea fines Google and Apple over app market practices
articles.title: South Korea fines Google and Apple over ‘unfair’ app market practices
articles.summary: South Korea fined Alphabet unit Google and Apple a combined 63.7 billion won on Wednesday for abusing app store dominance. The Korea Media and Communications Commission penalized Google 42.9 billion won and Apple 20.8 billion won for forcing developers onto proprietary payment systems and delaying app reviews. Regulators ordered both technology giants to permit external payment links and improve review procedures for local developers.
articles.description: The Commission fined Google 42.9 billion won ($32 million) and Apple 20.8 billion won ($15.5 million) and ordered both companies to let South Korean developers use external payment links within their apps and to improve their app review procedures

articles.headline: Cyclone leaves trail of destruction in India as thousands evacuated
articles.title: Cyclone leaves trail of destruction in India as thousands evacuated
articles.description: Cyclone Arnab has left a trail of destruction along India’s eastern coast.

articles.headline: Palestinian citizens of Israel turn out in high numbers for elections
articles.title: High voter turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel threatens Netanyahu
articles.summary: Palestinian citizens of Israel participated in parliamentary elections in unprecedented numbers, with certain towns reporting turnout rates exceeding 70 percent. The surge threatens to deny Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his right-wing coalition the 61-seat majority required to govern. Arab parties like the Joint List and the United Arab List could secure up to 17 combined seats, driven by voter opposition to current government policies and recent far-right campaigns.
articles.description: A historic turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel positions Arab parties as kingmakers against the far right.

articles.headline: Cabinet approves three percent dearness allowance hike for central employees
articles.title: Cabinet approves 3% hike in dearness allowance for central government employees
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a three percent increase in dearness allowance and dearness relief on October 28, 2026, benefiting over 1.17 crore central government employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated the hike is effective from July 1, 2026. Additionally, the Cabinet cleared the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme with a budgetary outlay of Rs 10,000 crore.
articles.description: The DA and DR increase will be effective from July 1, 2026 and will benefit 48.54 lakh employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners

articles.headline: UK Chancellor John Healey unveils the government budget amid rising inflation
articles.title: Burnham’s government unveils its first UK budget: What to expect
articles.summary: British Chancellor John Healey announced the government tax and spending plans in parliament on Wednesday, aiming to tackle high inflation, national debt exceeding 3 trillion pounds, and defense funding gaps. The budget introduces potential taxes on banks and online marketplaces to fund public services and regional mayoralties, while addressing economic challenges driven by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
articles.description: UK chancellor to present an autumn budget amid rising living costs and energy bills.

articles.headline: Israeli military forces continue incursions across the occupied West Bank
articles.title: Israeli forces continue West Bank raids as Hebron lockdown enters sixth day
articles.summary: The Israeli army pursued ongoing military raids in Hebron during its sixth day of lockdown, searching homes and restricting residents in the occupied West Bank. Troops also detained four individuals in Tulkarem, deployed tear gas in Beita, and raided properties in Burin, following a United Nations Relief and Works Agency warning regarding the displacement of nearly 5,000 Palestinians.
articles.description: UN agency expresses 'grave concern' in Hebron and warns of echoes of 2025 'Iron Wall' operation.

articles.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and rival Gadi Eisenkot face parliamentary deadlock
articles.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot face difficult paths to power as neither set to win majority
articles.summary: Early results from Israel's election on October 28, 2026, indicate Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party emerged as the largest faction, though his right-wing bloc falls just short of a majority. Former army chief Gadi Eisenkot also claims strong public support for change. Final outcomes remain uncertain pending the counting of absentee ballots, leaving both leaders facing complex coalition negotiations.
articles.description: The two main blocs appear to have too few seats to form the next government without reliance on Arab parties.

articles.headline: Democrats lead national polls as political figures campaign ahead of midterms
articles.title: US midterms: Six days left – who leads in the polls as Trump, Obama rally
articles.summary: Democrats hold a nine-point advantage over Republicans in national polling with six days remaining before the November 3 midterm elections in the United States. President Donald Trump campaigned in Texas and prepared for an Ohio rally, while former President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigned in Georgia amid competitive Senate contests across multiple states.
articles.description: Democrats lead national polls as Trump and Obama campaign in key states six days before the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Nordic leaders hold rare phone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin
articles.title: Norway and Finland hold rare phone call with Putin: What that means
articles.summary: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin for ninety minutes on Tuesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The rare diplomatic contact preceded United States-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi next month, although Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated the discussion offered nothing new.
articles.description: The two Nordic leaders are attempting to influence US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi to end the war in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Yemeni families struggle in Taiz amid severe road closures and soaring prices
articles.title: Mapping the siege of Yemen’s Taiz, and the price families are paying
articles.summary: Residents in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz face extreme shortages of food, water, and fuel following road closures in October 2026. The United Nations warned that restricted access and security issues are blocking vital supplies. Local father Yousef Farhan noted that his income stopped due to the siege, forcing his family to cook over firewood as prices for basic goods surge.
articles.description: Three weeks into the siege of Yemen’s third-largest city, prices have doubled, and families are down to the basics.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticizes business community silence amid leadership dispute at Tata Sons
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi says Tata Group ‘being criminally destroyed’, questions India Inc.’s ‘silence’
articles.summary: Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi accused the country's business class of silence while alleging the Tata Group is being criminally destroyed. The comments address a boardroom dispute regarding the potential stock exchange listing of Tata Sons, opposed by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata. The Tata Trusts hold approximately sixty-six percent shares in the holding company.
articles.description: The Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha also said “Indian business is not Modi and Shah’s plaything”

articles.headline: Ten people killed after two trains collide in central Spain near Urda
articles.title: Train collision in Spain kills at least 30 people
articles.summary: A collision between two trains in central Spain resulted in at least ten fatalities and the derailment of two carriages on October 28, 2026. Regional government spokeswoman Esther Padilla stated that a Renfe AVE high-speed train struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train near Urda in Toledo province. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez expressed shock as emergency medical teams and firefighters deployed to the site.
articles.description: Crash occurred near Urda in Toledo province, south of Madrid, on high-speed line connecting the capital with Seville.

articles.headline: Why the US midterms matter even if you don’t live in America
articles.title: Why the US midterms matter even if you don’t live in America
articles.description: From military aid and sanctions to trade and tariffs, the US midterms could shape decisions that affect millions.

articles.headline: Israelis vote in record numbers in general election
articles.title: Record turnout as Israeli voters deliver verdict on Netanyahu
articles.summary: Eligible citizens flocked to polling stations on October 27, 2026, creating the highest mid-day voter turnout since 1973 as the Central Elections Committee recorded 44.9 percent participation by early afternoon. The tense general election evaluated veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu against centrist challenger Gadi Eisenkot amid regional conflicts, security concerns, and reports of isolated voting irregularities and arrests.
articles.description: Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of October 7 and the multi-front regional wars that it sparked, with the trauma from the attack still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign

articles.headline: Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: At least 3 dead after Cylone Arnad hits southern India
articles.summary: Cyclone Arnab struck India's east coast on Wednesday morning with wind speeds reaching up to 135 kilometers per hour. Authorities evacuated at least 180,000 residents from Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, disrupting transport and shutting schools. While no casualties were reported, neighboring Nepal and Sri Lanka issued severe weather warnings for floods, landslides, and avalanches.
articles.description: Authorities evacuate 180,000 people as storm causes flooding, disrupting flights and train schedules.

articles.headline: Oil prices climb over one percent following refinery attack in Saudi Arabia
articles.title: Oil rises over 1% after Saudi Arabian refinery attack reignites supply risk
articles.summary: Global crude benchmarks increased by more than one percent on October 28, 2026, driven by renewed supply concerns after Yemen’s Houthis targeted a major Saudi Arabian facility with a missile. Brent crude futures rose to $115.47 a barrel. According to market sources, United States crude inventories also declined by 2.03 million barrels, while investors awaited official inventory data and an upcoming OPEC+ meeting.
articles.description: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said ‌they had hit Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with a missile, intensifying their strikes against ‌the world’s second-largest crude producer

articles.headline: UN nuclear chief reports no repairs at damaged Iranian nuclear sites
articles.title: Iran hasn't tried to repair nuclear facilities damaged in Israeli-U.S. strikes: IAEA chief
articles.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi stated on October 27, 2026, that there is no evidence Iran has attempted to repair nuclear facilities damaged by United States and Israeli strikes. Speaking at a United Nations Security Council meeting called by Western nations, Grossi urged Tehran to grant inspectors access. Meanwhile, Iranian officials condemned the military actions and criticized Western focus on Iran's nuclear program.
articles.description: During a UN Security Council meeting, Rafael Grossi urged Iran to give inspectors access to all nuclear sites, including those damaged in the military attacks; Iran maintains that its nuclear program is peaceful

articles.headline: Elderly women and children survive Russian attack on Kharkiv
articles.title: Elderly women and children survive Russian attack on Kharkiv
articles.description: A Russian drone attack in Ukraine's Kharkiv late Tuesday forced elderly women and children to evacuate their homes.

articles.headline: United States President Donald Trump rolls back oil and gas methane rules
articles.title: Trump drastically loosens oil and gas methane rules
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced the termination of regulations restricting methane emissions from oil and gas producers on October 27, 2026. Speaking at a rally in Lubbock, Texas, Trump stated the move will save $45 billion and boost fossil-fuel production. Environmental groups criticized the decision, warning it removes critical oversight from the world's leading methane-emitting sector.
articles.description: Mr. Trump is pushing ways of bringing down energy costs ahead of the midterms, amid voter anger over soaring oil costs caused by his war on Iran

articles.headline: Jio Platforms makes strong market debut with shares listing at premium
articles.title: Jio Platforms debuts on stock exchanges at premium of ₹1,358 per share
articles.summary: Jio Platforms Limited completed India's largest initial public offering on October 28, 2026, listing on the National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange at ₹1,358 per share. The ₹30,200 crore offering achieved a 21.36% premium over its issue price. The milestone elevates Jio to India's second-largest company by market capitalisation, reaching ₹12.5 lakh crore amid strong investor demand and positive broker outlooks.
articles.description: Jio becomes India’s second-largest company in terms of market capitalisation at ₹12.5 lakh crore, replacing Bharti Airtel

articles.headline: Federal Reserve expected to keep interest rates steady amid rising inflation
articles.title: Federal Reserve likely to skip rate hike despite elevated inflation
articles.summary: The United States Federal Reserve led by Chairman Kevin Warsh is anticipated to maintain interest rates on Wednesday October 28 2026 despite accelerated inflation driven by higher oil and gas prices from the Iran war. Consumer prices rose 3.7% in September. Economists warn above target inflation could persist for months affecting mortgage rates and the broader economy.
articles.description: The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, wants to return inflation to its 2% target, which it typically does by raising its short-term interest rate. Higher borrowing costs, over time, can cool spending and slow inflation

articles.headline: Watch: What happens now after close vote in Israeli election?
articles.title: Watch: What happens now after close vote in Israeli election?
articles.description: Polls have closed in the Israeli election, but there is no clear winner.

articles.headline: Israeli exit polls project narrow edge for opposition bloc in election
articles.title: First Israeli election exit polls show narrow edge for Opposition
articles.summary: Initial exit polls following Tuesday October 27 2026 elections in Israel project the opposition bloc winning 52 or 53 seats just short of a majority in the 120 seat Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu led Likud party remains the largest single party with 24 or 25 seats. Turnout was high with major gains for Arab majority parties Raam and the Joint List.
articles.description: Israel’s current Opposition chief Yair Lapid said Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a “crushing defeat”, while left-wing leader Yair Golan said the public had “fired the Netanyahu government”

articles.headline: More than 100 killed in Sudanese military drone strike on Nyala market
articles.title: More than 100 people killed in Sudanese army drone attack on market, says Sudanese rights group
articles.summary: Rights group Emergency Lawyers stated that a Sudanese military drone strike on a crowded market in Nyala killed over 100 people and injured 113 others on Monday October 26 2026. The conflict which began in April 2023 involves fighting between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces creating a severe humanitarian crisis affecting millions of citizens nationwide.
articles.description: At least 113 people injured in the attack; many of those killed and injured are women and children, a rights group says

articles.headline: Mathematician dispute highlights growing concerns over artificial intelligence in science
articles.title: A bust-up between mathematicians is fuelling fears that AI could undermine science
articles.summary: A disagreement involving mathematician Tristan Buckmaster regarding an artificial intelligence solution to the Navier Stokes equations has raised questions about research integrity. While firms like Google DeepMind utilize models such as AlphaFold to accelerate scientific discoveries critics warn that generative artificial intelligence could undermine trust by introducing hallucinations and distorting findings across research fields.
articles.description: AI has made some awesome scientific discoveries. But now, questions are being raised about its accuracy

articles.headline: Indian border police chief remarks spark political controversy over Chinese troops
articles.title: India and China were easing tensions - then a border official spoke out
articles.summary: Shatrujeet Singh Kapur director general of the Indo Tibetan Border Police stated that Chinese troops returned to disputed areas in Arunachal Pradesh pitching tents deep inside Indian claimed territory. The rare public remarks triggered political fallout in Delhi with opposition leaders criticizing Prime Minister Narendra Modi while foreign ministries from both nations addressed ongoing border management.
articles.description: India-China ties were on a cautious recovery path until a border official’s remarks raised fresh doubts about ground realities.

articles.headline: China supports more elderly people than children for first time
articles.title: China's families are now supporting more old people than kids
articles.summary: Official data released by the government reveals that the ratio of dependent elderly individuals in China reached twenty-three percent last year, exceeding the figure for children. This demographic shift highlights an ageing population that could strain healthcare and pension systems, driven by rapid urbanisation and the legacy of the former one-child policy.
articles.description: The latest figures mark a major milestone as Beijing grapples with an ageing population.

articles.headline: Ukraine ceasefire expands across Kherson region for humanitarian relief
articles.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
articles.summary: A truce initially established to deliver aid to Oleshky has been broadened throughout the wider Kherson region. Negotiated with international mediation, the agreement aims to facilitate mine-clearing operations and subsequent evacuations. Officials report that the cessation of hostilities is currently holding across the area without major incidents.
articles.description: The truce was originally planned for the stranded residents of Oleshky, and Russia and Ukraine say no breaches have been reported.

articles.headline: Studies show US voter fraud is extremely rare despite claims
articles.title: Trump says US voter fraud is 'rampant' - evidence suggests it is extremely rare
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has offered a one million dollar reward for reporting voter fraud convictions while alleging widespread cheating in postal voting and non-citizen participation. However, multiple studies and think tank databases indicate that actual instances of electoral fraud in the United States remain exceptionally uncommon.
articles.description: As the US president casts doubt on the security of the midterm elections, BBC Verify examines his claims.

articles.headline: What we know about Ukraine-Russia truce in Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.title: What we know about Ukraine-Russia truce in Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.description: The Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has had no electricity, gas or water for three years, as residents reported having to eat weeds to survive.

articles.headline: Indian defense scientists urge end-to-end domestic semiconductor manufacturing
articles.title: India must make its defence chips end-to-end, say scientists
articles.summary: Senior researchers speaking at a semiconductor summit warned that India's network-centric weapons remain vulnerable due to heavy reliance on imported microchips. Experts stressed the urgent necessity to develop complete domestic capabilities spanning design, materials, and fabrication to secure future military hardware against potential foreign compromise.

articles.description: The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 352.64 points, or 0.48%, to settle at 73,246.03, recovering most of its sharp intraday losses. During the day, it tumbled 995.1 points, or 1.35%, to 72,603.57

articles.headline: Registrar General directs officials to ensure accurate population enumeration in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Census 2027: Ensure every individual is counted, says Registrar General
articles.summary: Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan directed census officials in Andhra Pradesh to complete the second phase of Census 2027 accurately and within strict deadlines. Addressing principal census officers on October 9, 2026, Narayan emphasized the collection of sensitive data such as religion and caste under strict confidentiality. Chief Secretary G. Sai Prasad called for a comprehensive action plan to finish enumeration across 94,983 blocks within 55 days.
articles.description: Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan asks census officials in Andhra Pradesh to complete the second phase with accuracy and within deadlines

articles.headline: LTM launches GCC Origin to help enterprises establish global capability centres
articles.title: LTM launches GCC Origin as IT firms race to serve global capability centres
articles.summary: Technology services provider LTM launched GCC Origin, a dedicated business unit designed to help enterprises establish and transform global capability centres in India. Led by Shailendra Singh and reporting to Chief Executive Officer Venu Lambu, the unit formalizes the firm's previous offerings into a standalone business. The initiative integrates artificial intelligence, infrastructure, and talent acquisition to meet rising demand from multinational corporations for specialized technology operations.
articles.description: More than a year after introducing GCC-as-a-Service, LTM creates a dedicated business unit as TCS, Infosys and other technology companies expand their offerings for multinational firms setting up in-house centres

articles.headline: Rupee drops twenty-one paise to close at ninety-five point twenty-eight
articles.title: Rupee falls 21 paise to close at 95.28 against U.S. dollar
articles.summary: The Indian rupee depreciated by 21 paise to close provisionally at 95.28 against the U.S. dollar on October 28, 2026. According to forex traders, the decline was driven by a stronger U.S. dollar and surging crude oil prices. Meanwhile, the domestic equity market saw the Sensex decline by 352.64 points to settle at 73,246.03 during the trading session.
articles.description: In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 95.01 against the dollar, then lost ground to touch an intra-day low of 95.29 and finally settled for the day at 95.28 (provisional), registering a decline of 21 paise over its previous close

articles.headline: Hcltech introduces artificial intelligence nano Global Capability Centre offering on Amazon Web Services
articles.title: HCLTech launches AI-powered nano GCC offering on AWS
articles.summary: HCLTech has collaborated with Amazon Web Services to unveil an artificial intelligence powered nano Global Capability Centre model tailored for enterprises. The offering integrates advisory expertise and platforms with cloud infrastructure and agentic services to facilitate transitions. Targeting Asia-Pacific first, the initiative aims to provide scalable and lower-risk operational pathways according to company executives Kiran Cherukuri and Prabhakar Appana.
articles.description: New model targets enterprises seeking to build AI-native operations through smaller, focused teams, with Asia Pacific as the first phase of rollout

articles.headline: Jamia student protest enters seventeenth day amid university property damage allegations
articles.title: Jamia student protest: Varsity alleges damage to property as stir continues for 17th day
articles.summary: Students at Jamia Millia Islamia continued their agitation for the seventeenth day demanding the restoration of the student union, despite the administration offering to hold elections within fifteen days of approving the union constitution. University officials reported property damage on campus, while political figures including Congress leader Pawan Khera expressed support for the protesting students.
articles.description: Congress said students have the right to form a students’ union and that it stands in solidarity with their struggle

articles.headline: Abhishek Sharma claims top position in International Cricket Council men's Twenty20 batting rankings
articles.title: Abhishek Sharma topples Ishan Kishan to become world No. 1 batter in T20I rankings
articles.summary: Indian opening batter Abhishek Sharma reclaimed the world number one spot in the International Cricket Council men's Twenty20 International rankings following a century against New Zealand in Wellington. He surpassed teammate Ishan Kishan, who missed matches due to injury. Meanwhile, South Africa's Marco Jansen ascended to become the top-ranked Test all-rounder and bowler, overtaking Ravindra Jadeja and Mitchell Starc.
articles.description: Abhishek hammered his fourth T20I century on October 27, smashing 113 off just 38 balls in the third T20I to power India to a six-wicket win

articles.headline: Supreme Court permits petition regarding pre-loaded caste menu for Census 2027
articles.title: Supreme Court allows petitioner seeking pre-loaded drop-down caste menu in Census to approach Registrar General
articles.summary: The Supreme Court granted the OBC Federation of India permission to approach the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India regarding a pre-loaded drop-down menu for recognised Other Backward Classes in Census 2027 digital tools. The petitioner argued that open text fields lead to inaccuracies, while the Chief Justice noted that granular operational decisions form part of policy-making.
articles.description: Article 342A specifically identifies SEBCs; over ₹11,000 crore has been budgeted for Census 2027, but a drop-down menu is lacking, counsel for the petitioner, the OBC Federation of India, says

articles.headline: Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil returns to Columbia after US detention
articles.title: Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil returns to Columbia after US detention
articles.description: Pro-Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil returned to Columbia University for the first time since his US detention.

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party leader faces criticism following participation in Buddhist conversion ceremony in Delhi
articles.title: A Delhi event unveils fault lines in the Dalit-OBC formulation of SP politics
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati faced backlash from the Bharatiya Janata Party and reprimands from party leadership after reciting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's twenty-two vows during a Buddhist ceremony in Delhi. The incident exposed internal political tensions regarding numerical caste aggregation formulas and cultural associations with Hindu deities within Uttar Pradesh politics ahead of upcoming elections.
articles.description: The brouhaha over Rajkumar Bhati reciting Ambedkar’s vows shows the limits of the SP’s revival of the Lohiate policy of numerical aggregation

articles.headline: Bharatiya Janata Party secures five seats in Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections
articles.title: Uttar Pradesh MLC polls: BJP wins five seats, SP three; counting underway
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party secured five seats while the Samajwadi Party won three in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council elections, according to officials on Wednesday. Vote counting continued across constituencies following the October 23, 2026 polling. The results serve as a crucial indicator ahead of the upcoming 2027 state assembly elections, amidst political disputes over counting procedures and candidate treatment.
articles.description: The counting is underway in Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut, Jhansi, Bareilly and Gorakhpur

articles.headline: India bloc schedules public impeachment event for Chief Election Commissioner
articles.title: INDIA bloc's 'public impeachment' of CEC to be held at Kharge's residence on October 30
articles.summary: The Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance will conduct a public impeachment event targeting Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at the official residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge in New Delhi on Friday. Opposition leaders stated the programme was relocated after facing administrative obstacles at alternative venues, serving as a prelude to a larger November 1 rally addressing electoral roll revisions.
articles.description: The Congress president’s official residence was decided as the venue after the Opposition bloc’s attempts to organise the event at the Ashok Hotel and Ramlila Maidan allegedly ran into hurdles over permissions

articles.headline: Municipal Corporation issues water advisory for parts of Mumbai and Thane
articles.title: Boil, filter drinking water for seven days: BMC tells residents in parts of Mumbai, Thane and Bhiwandi
articles.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation advised residents across multiple wards in Mumbai, Thane, and Bhiwandi to boil and filter drinking water for seven days. Issued on Tuesday, the precautionary directive follows water quality concerns arising from the recommissioning of a repaired reservoir at the Pise-Panjrapur supply complex, though no actual contamination has been officially confirmed by civic authorities.
articles.description: The BMC issued the warning over a possible impact on water quality following the recommissioning of a repaired reservoir at the Pise-Panjrapur water supply complex

articles.headline: Odisha districts face flash flood alerts as cyclone Arnab passes coast
articles.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: Flash flood alert for several southern Odisha districts amid heavy rain
articles.summary: Several southern Odisha districts are bracing for flash floods after cyclone Arnab moved past the Andhra Pradesh coast, prompting heavy rainfall and district alerts from the India Meteorological Department. State officials reported that nearly 28,000 residents have been evacuated across eight districts, with disaster response forces deployed to manage rising water levels and potential river impacts.
articles.description: Around 28,000 people had been evacuated across eight districts so far, against a planned evacuation target of 48,000, as per Odisha Special Relief Commissioner

articles.headline: Tanzania announces natural gas discovery in Mnazi Bay
articles.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
articles.summary: Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation and French firm Maurel and Prom discovered 223 billion cubic feet of natural gas at the Kasa-1X ST2 well in Mnazi Bay. Energy Minister Juma Homera stated the find will boost domestic supplies as demand grows. Production is scheduled to begin next month to support the East African nation's energy needs and economic activities.
articles.description: The energy minister described it as a "major milestone" for the East African nation.

articles.headline: Serbian police shoot dead attacker outside Israeli embassy
articles.title: Serbian shot dead after attacking officer outside Israeli embassy, minister says
articles.summary: Serbian police shot dead a minor who rushed an officer with two knives outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade. Interior Minister Ivica Dacic stated the suspect was known as an Islamic State supporter. The officer sustained a minor facial wound, and authorities raised the national terrorism threat level to a red alert while investigations continue.
articles.description: Authorities say the attacker in Belgrade was an underage male who was being monitored by security services.

articles.headline: Hormuz oil spill forces closure of UAE beaches
articles.title: Hormuz oil spill forces closure of UAE beaches
articles.description: An oil spill from a damaged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz has reached the UAE’s beaches, forcing their closure.

articles.headline: Tel Aviv index drops as Israeli election exit polls show no winner
articles.title: Israel’s stock market drops as exit polls show no clear election winner
articles.summary: Israel's benchmark stock index fell up to 3.5 percent in early trading after exit polls indicated no clear parliamentary majority following the national election. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition and the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot both fell short of the sixty-one seats required, with vote counting ongoing across the country.
articles.description: Benchmark Tel Aviv 125 index falls more than 3 percent amid uncertainty over who will lead the next government.

articles.headline: Lula da Silva secures fourth presidential term in Brazil amid climate challenges
articles.title: Lula’s win gives Brazil an opportunity to cement its climate leadership, but challenges remain
articles.summary: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured his fourth term as Brazil's president, presenting opportunities for international climate leadership alongside domestic and regional governance hurdles. Brazil continues to navigate Amazonian deforestation and regional cooperation through the Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organisation, while financial pledges for the Tropical Forest Forever Facility approach the ten billion dollar target.
articles.description: In his fourth term, the President can potentially negotiate across the divides that currently frustrate climate agreements, given his country’s status as Latin America’s largest economy, host to most of the Amazon, and its diplomatic relationships with the EU, the U.S., China, the BRICS countries and other devel

articles.headline: Israeli right-wing leaders make provocative statements during election vote counting
articles.title: Israeli right makes provocative statements as election votes are counted
articles.summary: Senior figures on the Israeli right made controversial remarks regarding Arab voters and potential settlements in Gaza as exit polls indicated Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing alliance faced setbacks. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Netanyahu raised concerns about high turnout in Arab communities, while police arrested three individuals for alleged voter bribery. Netanyahu fell short of a majority, leaving Arab-led parties in a potentially decisive role for the next government formation.
articles.description: Netanyahu and Smotrich rail against Arab voters as rival political camps face an uncertain path to power.

articles.headline: Policeman shoots dead knife attacker outside Israeli embassy in Belgrade
articles.title: Policeman kills knife attacker outside Israeli embassy in Serbia
articles.summary: A Serbian police officer fatally shot an unidentified armed assailant outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade after being attacked with two knives and wounded in the left cheek. Outgoing Interior Minister Ivica Dacic stated that the attacker rushed the guard house while shouting religious phrases. Following the incident, Serbia raised its security threat level to red and increased police presence at key locations across the country.
articles.description: It is the second such attack at the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in two years. In June 2024, an ‌assailant shot a Serbian police officer in the neck with ​a crossbow

articles.headline: Canada and United Arab Emirates sign comprehensive trade deal
articles.title: Canada signs trade deal with UAE in push for non-US markets
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan signed the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement to lower trade barriers and boost investment. The pact aims to eliminate tariffs on over 99 percent of Canadian exports to the United Arab Emirates and address non-tariff measures. The agreement forms part of Carney's broader strategy to expand non-US trade amid ongoing economic tensions with Washington.
articles.description: The agreement aims to cut tariffs, reduce red tape and improve market access for businesses in both countries.

articles.headline: Is AIPAC losing its grip on US politics?
articles.title: Is AIPAC losing its grip on US politics?
articles.description: Pro-Israel lobby, AIPAC, is changing its strategy, ending candidate endorsements and direct campaign contributions.

articles.headline: Kenyan family protests extradition hearing delay for former soldier
articles.title: Anger in Kenya over extradition hearing delay for ex-British soldier accused of murdering woman
articles.summary: Relatives of Agnes Wanjiru expressed outrage after a UK extradition hearing for Robert James Purkiss, a former British soldier accused of murdering her in 2012, was postponed until May 2027. The victim's niece criticized the lack of official explanation. Purkiss denies the allegation and is fighting extradition from the United Kingdom to face trial in Kenya.
articles.description: No official reason has been given for postponing next month’s hearing to May 2027, the family says.

articles.headline: Stan Wawrinka ends professional tennis career with defeat in Basel
articles.title: Former world No 3 Stan Wawrinka ends career in home match defeat in Basel
articles.summary: Three-time major champion Stan Wawrinka concluded his 24-year professional tennis career following a first-round defeat at the Basel Open against Czech player Jiri Lehecka. The 41-year-old Swiss player received a warm farewell from the partisan home crowd after losing in straight sets. Wawrinka secured three Grand Slam titles during his career and plans to participate in an exhibition farewell event in Geneva in December alongside other tennis stars.
articles.description: Stan Wawrinka, one of few players to win multiple Grand Slams in era dominated by Federer, Nadal and Djokovic, retires.

articles.headline: Why is the system failing France’s younger generation?
articles.title: Why is the system failing France’s younger generation?
articles.description: Why are French youth rioting?

articles.headline: U.S. defense secretary proposes new defence framework at Philippine summit
articles.title: Hegseth proposes 'ambitious' U.S.-ASEAN defence framework at Philippine summit
articles.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth proposed creating a new U.S.-ASEAN defence framework during a meeting in Cebu on October 28, 2026. Speaking before Association of Southeast Asian Nations defence chiefs, Mr. Hegseth urged regional partners to enhance maritime domain awareness and naval cooperation. The proposal aims to navigate upcoming years amid ongoing regional tensions in the South China Sea.
articles.description: The United States has been seeking to boost its regional defence partnerships in recent years, citing the need to uphold what it terms a "free and open Indo-Pacific" as China has increasingly flexed its muscles in the region

articles.headline: Fleetwood Town eliminates Arsenal from League Cup in penalty shootout
articles.title: Carabao Cup: Arsenal knocked out by fourth-tier Fleetwood in shootout
articles.summary: League Two side Fleetwood Town defeated Arsenal 5-3 on penalties following a 1-1 draw in the League Cup last 16 on October 27, 2026. Aaron Loupalo-Bi opened the scoring for Fleetwood before Viktor Gyokeres equalized for Arsenal. Following a red card to Arsenal teenager Max Dowman, Fleetwood goalkeeper Lynch saved a penalty in the shootout to secure a quarterfinal spot.
articles.description: The victory was a remarkable result for Fleetwood, ​who sit in the bottom half of League Two and had won only one of their ⁠previous eight league matches

articles.headline: Supreme Court agrees to hear petition challenging industry definition in law
articles.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear challenge to definition of ‘industry’ in new Central law
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India agreed on October 28, 2026, to hear a petition filed by the All India Trade Union Congress Tamil Nadu challenging the Industrial Relations Code 2020. The trade union argues that the law defines industry vaguely while exempting charitable and sovereign government functions, raising significant concerns regarding legal protections for workers across the country.
articles.description: The All India Trade Union Congress Tamil Nadu’s petition challenged the definition of ‘industry’ under the Industrial Relations Code (IRC) 2020 as “deliciously vague”; The senior counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan said the definition in the IRC Code did not meet the requirements of the ‘triple test’

articles.headline: Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav found dead in Delhi
articles.title: Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav found dead
articles.summary: Asian Para Games gold medallist Neeraj Yadav was found dead at his Delhi residence on October 28, 2026. The 42-year-old para-athlete, who competed in the F55 category, was reportedly under emotional stress following a doping suspension that forced him to miss the recent games in Aichi-Nagoya. A post-mortem examination is currently underway at a local hospital.
articles.description: The 42-year-old Yadav, who won three gold medals in the 2018 Jakarta Games, had missed the recent Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya due to a doping suspension

articles.headline: Arsenal suffers shock defeat against Fleetwood Town in League Cup
articles.title: Where does Arsenal’s Fleetwood humiliation place in English cup shocks?
articles.summary: Premier League champions Arsenal suffered a stunning fourth-round defeat in the League Cup against fourth-tier Fleetwood Town on October 27, 2026. The match ended in a one-all draw before Fleetwood triumphed five-three on penalties. This historic upset ranks among the most remarkable shocks in English football, mirroring previous giant-killing moments in domestic cup history.
articles.description: How big a shock is the Premier League champions' 5-3 defeat on penalties after a 1-1 draw with a fourth-tier club?

articles.headline: Donald Trump approves visas for Flavio Bolsonaro following election defeat
articles.title: Trump would approve Flavio Bolsonaro coming to U.S.; says Brazil election was ‘very strange’
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated on October 28, 2026, that he approves of Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family receiving visas to enter the United States. Bolsonaro departed Brazil following his defeat in the presidential election against incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Trump also criticized the Brazilian election process during remarks at Joint Base Andrews.
articles.description: Asked about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin ​Netanyahu’s party losing seats in elections, Mr. Trump said he had heard that Mr. Netanyahu did very well

articles.headline: Stan Wawrinka ends professional tennis career with defeat in Basel
articles.title: Wawrinka brings career to a close with defeat in Basel
articles.summary: Three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka concluded his professional tennis career on October 27, 2026, after losing in straight sets to Czech player Jiri Lehecka at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. The 41-year-old Swiss player retires after 24 years on the tour, having secured sixteen Association of Tennis Professionals titles and multiple major championships throughout his distinguished career.
articles.description: Wawrinka announced ‌last year that he would retire at the end of ‌the 2026 season, 24 years after ‌he ⁠turned professional

articles.headline: UAE President honours Indian pilot and flydubai crew for bravery
articles.title: Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, flydubai crew honoured by UAE President for bravery during mid-air attack
articles.summary: United Arab Emirates President His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II on Indian Captain Smit Machchhar and flydubai crew members on October 27, 2026. The award recognises their efforts during a September 30 cockpit attack on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, where an Omani co-pilot stabbed the captain before passengers and crew intervened.
articles.description: The medals were presented by His Highness Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence

articles.headline: Tennis player Novak Djokovic praises Serbia student movement election victory
articles.title: Tennis great Novak Djokovic praises Serbia's student movement after stunning election win
articles.summary: Serbian tennis player Novak Djokovic expressed deep respect for Serbia's youth movement during a press conference on October 27, 2026, at the Swiss Indoors in Basel. He praised the students for showing resilience and dignity over two years of pressure following their victory against longtime strongman Aleksandar Vucic, who conceded defeat on October 25, 2026.
articles.description: Aleksander Vucic conceded defeat to a student-led opposition movement on October 25; Novak Djokovic says, the youth movement managed to create a sense of pride in all the people, not just in Serbia but abroad as well

articles.headline: Indian stock markets decline nearly one percent amid rising crude prices
articles.title: Markets plunge nearly 1%; rise in crude, FOMC decision weigh on investor sentiments
articles.summary: The Indian stock market dropped almost one percent on October 28, 2026, driven by higher crude oil prices and investor caution ahead of the United States Federal Open Market Committee policy decision. Benchmark Brent crude futures rose about 1.5 percent to 115.36 dollars per barrel following a Houthi attack on a Saudi Arabian oil refinery.
articles.description: Global investors also remain cautious ahead of the U.S. FOMC decision due later in day. The U.S. central bank is widely expected to keep the Fed Funds target range unchanged at 3.75%-4.00%

articles.headline: Ministry amends motor vehicle rules to permit ethanol-based fuels up to one hundred percent
articles.title: What the new E100 vehicle rules mean | Explained
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways amended the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to allow vehicles to use fuels containing up to 100 percent ethanol. The regulatory changes support the rollout of flex-fuel vehicles and official homologation processes while clarifying that owners of existing vehicles are not required to switch or modify their current engines.
articles.description: The amendments modify Rule 115, which deals with emission standards and related requirements for motor vehicles, and Rule 115E, which contains additional provisions relating to emission testing

articles.headline: King Charles acknowledges historic suffering during Caribbean tour commencement
articles.title: King acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins
articles.summary: King Charles III began a nine-day Caribbean tour on October 27, 2026, by acknowledging historic injustices and the great suffering of the past during an event in the Bahamas. Meeting with Prime Minister Philip Edward Davis and Governor General Dame Cynthia A. Pratt, the monarch faced protests calling for slavery reparations ahead of the upcoming Commonwealth summit.
articles.description: The King is on a nine-day tour that will take him to three countries, including the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda.

articles.headline: Two British nationals charged in connection with incident at RAF Fairford
articles.title: Two Britons charged in connection with assisting Iran over U.K. airbase incident
articles.summary: Nouman Essghir and Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, both 24 years old from London, were charged under the United Kingdom National Security Act following an incident at the Royal Air Force Fairford airbase on September 27, 2026. According to U.K. authorities, the suspects approached the base in three vans, prompting local evacuations. British officials linked Tehran to the plot, which led the United States to temporarily remove its bombers from the facility, though Iran denied any involvement.
articles.description: British-Iranian dual national Mohmed Abdulkarim and British citizen Nouman Essghir, both aged 24 and from London, were charged under the National Security Act, U.K. prosecutors say

articles.headline: U.S. and Cuban representatives clash during UN General Assembly debate
articles.title: U.S., Cuba shouting match derails debate at UN
articles.summary: A heated shouting match between United States Ambassador Mike Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez led to the temporary suspension of debate at the United Nations General Assembly on October 27, 2026. The confrontation erupted during discussions on a resolution demanding an end to the U.S. embargo against Cuba, a measure coinciding with intensified American economic pressure and recent diplomatic friction between Washington and Havana.
articles.description: The row broke out during debate on a resolution calling for an end to the U.S. embargo on its communist-led neighbour, a non-binding measure which Cuba has put forward every year since 1992

articles.headline: Marco Rubio joins Donald Trump on campaign trail in Texas
articles.title: Rubio joins Trump on campaign trail days before U.S. midterms
articles.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio made a rare appearance alongside President Donald Trump in Corpus Christi, Texas, on October 27, 2026, visiting an oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude just days before the midterm elections. The joint appearance occurred as Republicans navigate voter concerns over inflation and energy costs following global oil price surges tied to earlier U.S. and Israeli strikes targeting Iran.
articles.description: Donald Trump called Marco Rubio on stage at his campaign rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, remarking: “He’s so popular”

articles.headline: Alexander brothers sentenced to thirty years in prison for sex trafficking
articles.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison in sex trafficking case
articles.summary: Tal Alexander and his twin brothers Oren and Alon Alexander were each sentenced to 30 years in prison by Judge Valerie Caproni in New York on October 27, 2026. The three men were convicted in March of utilizing their wealth and status to lure, drug, and sexually assault dozens of women and minors over decades, following a trial where multiple victims testified regarding the ongoing psychological trauma they endured.
articles.description: The trio - two of whom were high-profile US real estate moguls - were found guilty using their social status to lure women to parties and then raping them.

articles.headline: Researchers criticize OpenAI over restricted release of scientific breakthroughs
articles.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
articles.summary: OpenAI announced major advancements in mathematics, computer science, and physics on October 26, 2026, alongside a strategy utilizing expert shepherds to determine how findings are shared. Academic researchers expressed frustration with the company for restricting early access and gatekeeping results concerning complex problems like the Kakeya conjecture, arguing that publicly announced scientific findings must be fully made available for immediate community scrutiny.
articles.description: On Monday, OpenAI announced impressive breakthroughs in mathematics, computer science, and physics, along with what the company says is an evolving approach to communicating its findings. But despite its apparent course correction, researchers who spoke to The Verge are growing increasingly tired of the company's antics. It has been a turbulent few months between OpenAI […]

articles.headline: Egyptian court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders Mada Masr closure
articles.title: Egypt court fines journalist Lina Attalah and orders news site's closure
articles.summary: The New Cairo Misdemeanours Court convicted Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah of managing an unlicensed website, imposing a three million Egyptian pound fine and ordering the independent news outlet's closure. Amnesty International and the Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the verdict as a severe blow to press freedom, while Attalah's legal team challenged an additional in absentia prison sentence.
articles.description: Amnesty International said the verdict against Attalah and independent outlet Mada Masr represented "a crushing blow to press freedom".

articles.headline: Lancashire parts ways with record-breaking fast bowler James Anderson
articles.title: Snapping ties abruptly with a match made in heaven
articles.summary: Lancashire abruptly ended a twenty-six-year association with 42-year-old fast bowler James Anderson, leaving members and supporters outraged by the sudden departure. Anderson, who took his fiftieth wicket of the 2025 season on September 15 against Kent, had recently assumed the role of full-time team captain following a historic career as Test cricket's most prolific fast-bowling wicket-taker.
articles.description: When he dismissed Kent’s Zimbabwean batter Tawanda Muyeye for his third scalp of the innings and his 50th of the season on September 15, James Anderson would hardly have imagined that it would be his final wicket for Lancashire

articles.headline: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urges state governments to adopt prudent borrowing strategies
articles.title: RBI Governor asks states to adopt prudent borrowing strategies
articles.summary: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra advised finance secretaries from twenty-seven states and three union territories to prioritize long-term fiscal health through prudent borrowing and quality spending. Speaking at the thirty-sixth Conference of State Finance Secretaries in October 2026, he also encouraged the adoption of the Unified Lending Interface and programmable central bank digital currency for direct benefit transfers.
articles.description: Addressing the 36th Conference of State Finance Secretaries, the governor also advised states to make effective use of the State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC) forum

articles.headline: Anthropic proposes complex governance structure ahead of initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic plans to go public with a novel governance framework designed to shield its social mission from commercial pressures. Legal experts note that the structure combines a public benefit corporation designation, a long-term benefit trust to appoint directors, and a founder-controlled entity holding majority voting power to maintain safety priorities despite shareholder expectations.
articles.description: Anthropic wants to have it both ways. With its impending IPO, it wants to tap the vast riches of the public markets and insists it doesn't want to compromise its core mission of developing AI safely and for the benefit of humanity. But greater model capabilities bring greater risks, and shareholders eager for returns may […]

articles.headline: Icra projects rise in fresh bad loans for Indian banking sector in FY27
articles.title: Fresh bad-loan generation may rise in FY27; private banks face greater pressure: Report
articles.summary: Ratings agency Icra projected an increase in fresh non-performing assets for the Indian banking sector during the current fiscal year, with private sector banks facing higher pressure due to unsecured retail and micro, small and medium enterprise loans. State-owned banks are expected to generate one lakh crore rupees in fresh bad loans compared to one point three lakh crore rupees for private banks.
articles.description: Ratings agency Icra expects the trend of relatively higher loan slippages at private sector banks to continue in the second half of FY27, even as credit costs are projected to remain favourable and significantly below historical levels

articles.headline: Google announces Genie 4 AI model with real-time prompt updates
articles.title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
articles.summary: Google announced the Genie 4 world model on Monday, introducing features such as real-time updates via natural language prompts, audio generation, and a simulation duration of about two minutes. Powered by Gemini 3.8 Flash, the model aims to assist filmmakers, game developers, and roboticists. Google stated that Genie 4 will soon launch as a research preview for trusted testers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.
articles.description: Google announced today its Genie 4 world model for generating interactive experiences using AI. The company says the model has four main updates: It allows for more realistic worlds, lets users update an experience in real time with a natural language prompt, can generate audio, and uses Gemini 3.8 Flash under the hood to help […]

articles.headline: Larsen & Toubro reports 33 percent rise in second-quarter net profit
articles.title: L&T Q2 PAT rises 33% to ₹5,202 crore, revenue up 16%
articles.summary: Larsen & Toubro reported a thirty-three percent year-on-year increase in consolidated profit after tax to 5,202 crore rupees for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. According to the company, consolidated revenue rose sixteen percent to 78,750 crore rupees, driven by execution across Projects, Products and Manufacturing businesses. Chairman and Managing Director S N Subrahmanyan stated that the performance reflects customer confidence despite changing geopolitical landscapes.
articles.description: L&T’s consolidated order book stood at ₹8,53,514 crore as of September 30, 2026, up 15% from March 2026. International orders accounted for 54% of the total order book, providing substantial revenue visibility.

articles.headline: AM Green signs long-term green ammonia supply agreement with JERA
articles.title: AM Green bags long term contract from JERA to supply green ammonia in Japan
articles.summary: AM Green Ammonia India entered into a binding heads of agreement to supply approximately 70,000 tonnes of green ammonia annually over five years to Japan's JERA Company. The green ammonia will be produced at AM Green's facility in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, which is planned for commissioning by 2028-29. Mahesh Kolli, Group President and Joint Managing Director, stated that the agreement supports Japan and the maritime industry's decarbonisation ambitions.
articles.description: AM Green will supply around 70,000 tonnes of green ammonia annually over five years, with the potential to extend the term for additional supply.

articles.summary: Maruti Suzuki India Limited reported a twenty-seven percent year-on-year decline in net profit to 2,414.9 crore rupees for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, due to mark-to-market losses and conflict impacts. Chairman R.C. Bhargava stated during a conference call that total sales volume rose 26.5 percent to 696,654 units, supported by strong domestic demand and expanding sport utility vehicle sales. The company also approved the incorporation of a Section 8 company to establish the Osamu Suzuki Centre of Excellence.
articles.description: Demand continued to outstrip supply, leaving the company with network inventory of about 17 days and pending bookings of approximately 265,000 units

articles.summary: Presenters Kate Scott and Thierry Henry dedicated the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London to Christophe Gleizes, a 37-year-old French sports journalist serving a seven-year prison sentence in Algeria. Arrested in May 2024 while reporting on a football club in Kabylie, Gleizes was accused of supporting terrorism and possessing harmful publications. Reporters Without Freedom campaigned for his release, while Algerian authorities have not yet commented on the tribute.
articles.description: He is in jail accused of supporting terrorism after travelling to the politically sensitive region Kabylie.
